newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Lion "surprised" by takeover rumour.
newsitem.headline: Lion "surprised" by takeover rumour.

text.p: Lion Nathan Ltd chief financial officer Alan Dickson said on Wednesday he could neither confirm nor deny rumours of a full or partial takeover bid for the company by Philip Morris Cos Inc.

"I really can't confirm or deny that," Dickson told Reuters. "It would catch me really by surprise if it were true. I don't know whether there's any substance to it or not. I'm actually trying to contact (managing director) Douglas Myers to find out if he knows anything about it. But I can't really shed any light one way or the other at the moment."
Lion shares were up 12 cents at NZ$3.62 in a weak market.

Earlier, shares in the brewing company were up 15 cents at $3.65. The rise was in contrast to the top-40 index, which at 12.35 p.m. (2335 GMT) was down 6.79 points at 2,401.49 with all other leading issues weaker.
"People are saying that Philip Morris has interest in Doug Myers' stake in Lion," said a broker who declined to be named.
"That's been sufficient to see the price the best part of 20 cents better."
Lion shares have climbed from a recent low of $3.32 on December 19. They ended 1996 at $3.39.
Dickson said Myers' stake in Lion, which is Australasia's biggest brewing company, was around 16-17 percent.
Another broker also said rumours were circulating in the market about a full or partial takeover bid for the company.
"Philip Morris has been mentioned," he said. "But it's rumours only." -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
